# The Recursive Stack: current brief

Cycle 0 · as of 2026-11-19 · next sweep due 2026-11-22 · 37 active signals

> **Inference optimisation is turning from a craft into a search.** Agents rewrite the serving stack against replayed real traffic: one model, one workload, one chip at a time.

Serving a large language model is its own engineering discipline: kernels that run on the chip, an engine that batches requests, a scheduler that decides which machine does what. Until recently people tuned all of it by hand, once per model. During 2026, teams began handing that work to coding agents that profile the stack, rewrite parts of it, measure the result on real traffic and keep what wins. This page tracks that change: who is doing it, what the evidence shows, where the claims outrun the evidence, and whether your own reading of it is holding up. An agent re-examines it every three days.

## Five things to know

- **Ten teams have announced the same loop since October.** Agents that profile an engine, rewrite part of it, measure, and keep what wins. Providers, both open engines, academics and one customer. Fourteen more teams described versions earlier. ([Inferact](https://inferact.ai/news/building-autonomous-inference-system), [Together AI](https://www.together.ai/blog/together-compiler-continual-compilation-for-ai-inference), [agenteconomics.org](https://agenteconomics.org/posts/inference-forge), [vLLM project](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-16-kimi-k3-megakernel))
- **It fits the stack to what you have.** The best kernels and settings differ by model, traffic and chip. Agents now regenerate them per combination, on NVIDIA, AMD, in-house and phone chips alike. ([Together AI](https://www.together.ai/blog/road-to-together-compiler), [Inferact](https://inferact.ai/news/building-autonomous-inference-system), [Shengjun Kris Dong](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04104), [Meta](https://engineering.fb.com/2026/04/02/developer-tools/kernelevolve-how-metas-ranking-engineer-agent-optimizes-ai-infrastructure/))
- **A public benchmark gave them a hill to climb.** AgentX replays real coding-agent sessions. Nearly every result is stated against it, and agent traffic rewards different optimisations than chat did. ([SemiAnalysis](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/agentx-inferencexv3-does-cuda-moat), [vLLM team and Inferact](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-09-08-vllm-agentx))
- **Measuring is now harder than optimising.** Kernel speed-ups of several times shrink to almost nothing inside a full engine. Some agent runs game the benchmark. Patches arrive faster than people can review them. ([Snowflake AI Research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23215), [ELLIS Institute Tübingen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20468), [Together AI](https://www.together.ai/blog/road-to-together-compiler))
- **Not yet recursive, and the commons keeps up.** The loops are bounded hillclimbs with goals set by people; nothing compounds yet. Specialised wins reach vLLM and SGLang within weeks, and per-customer tuning has bought tens of percent. ([Z.ai](https://z.ai/blog/glm-built-its-inference-infrastructure), [University of Chicago](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04646), [Inferact and the vLLM team](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-23-deepseek-v41-flash-pd-wide-ep), [Modal](https://modal.com/blog/trillion-tokens-trillion-parameters))

## Course check

**Your working framing:** Inference optimisation is moving toward a stack that fits itself to what you have (your workload, your models, your devices), and it is happening because LLMs are getting good at things like recursive self-improvement.

| Part of the framing | Verdict | In one line |
|---|---|---|
| Fits your workload | holding | Strong evidence. So far the workload is a class, not a person. |
| Fits each user | sharpen | Worth 20 to 45% so far. Most gains are class-level and shared. |
| Fits what you have | holding | The best kernels and settings change with the model and the chip in hand. |
| Driven by RSI | sharpen | Driven by bounded agent hillclimbs. Nothing has been shown to compound. |

**Sharper version:** Inference optimisation is turning from hand-craft into search. Agents rewrite kernels and engine paths against replayed real traffic, so the thing being optimised shrinks from a model to what you actually have: this model, this traffic shape, this chip, this month. The scarce asset is not the agent but the rig that tells you whether a change is real.

**Read next:**

- [Last year we built megakernels. This year we deleted them](https://www.together.ai/blog/road-to-together-compiler): The best single explanation of why measuring is harder than optimising. Read the sections on benchmarks lying and on their own ablations.
- [InferenceBench: open-ended LLM inference optimization by AI agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20468): The strongest counter-argument, from people with nothing to sell. Read it before taking any vendor number at face value.
- [Building an autonomous inference system](https://inferact.ai/news/building-autonomous-inference-system): The whole loop laid out by the people who maintain vLLM, including the parts they say they cannot do yet.

## Claims

| | Claim | Confidence | For / mixed / against |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Given a harness built by people, coding agents now find and land inference optimisations that survive end-to-end measurement in production engines. | 70% | 11 / 5 / 3 |
| C2 | The best serving configuration depends on what you are running: the traffic shape, the model and the chip. Kernels and settings tuned for one combination leave double-digit gains unclaimed on another, and all three keep changing. | 80% | 18 / 2 / 0 |
| C3 | Tuning the stack to one customer's own traffic is worth enough over a well-tuned class-level stack to justify doing it per customer, continuously. | 35% | 3 / 6 / 4 |
| C4 | Proposing optimisations has become cheap. Knowing whether one is real (on realistic inputs, end to end, with outputs intact) is the binding constraint, together with the human review that still gates what ships. | 80% | 16 / 3 / 0 |
| C5 | The optimisation loop is becoming recursive: the models being served power the agents that optimise their serving, the agents improve their own process, and gains compound from one cycle to the next. | 30% | 7 / 3 / 3 |
| C6 | New model architectures and new chips now arrive faster than people can hand-tune for them. That, more than agent capability, is what makes an automated loop necessary. | 70% | 9 / 1 / 0 |
| C7 | Open engines absorb specialised wins within weeks, so a private performance lead over upstream vLLM or SGLang is short-lived. | 55% | 7 / 0 / 2 |

## The numbers that carry the argument

**A kernel speed-up, before and after honest measurement.** Gains of several times shrink to about nothing.

- Best agent on FastKernels: 6.6x → 1.25x ([Snowflake AI Research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23215))
- Kernel-Smith kernel in SGLang: 4.78x → 1.02x ([Shanghai AI Laboratory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28342))
- SGLang kernel group: 2.03x → 1.02x ([SGLang team](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-02-agent-assisted-sglang-development/))
- Best model on KernelBench: 1.43x → 0.88x ([Meta](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16241))

**Agents against plain search at tuning a server.** With the same two hours, a simple parameter search still wins.

- Default vLLM: 4.05x ([ELLIS Institute Tübingen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20468))
- Best agent, May paper: 8.08x ([ELLIS Institute Tübingen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20468))
- Matched search, May paper: 11.53x ([ELLIS Institute Tübingen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20468))
- Best agent, November board: 12.08x ([ELLIS Institute Tübingen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20468))
- Best search composite, November: 14.3x ([ELLIS Institute Tübingen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20468))

**What specialising buys, by how narrow it is.** Tuning to a workload class buys multiples. Tuning to one customer has bought tens of percent.

- Cache-aware routing, code generation: 2.9x ([llm-d](https://llm-d.ai/blog/sticky-until-saturated-token-aware-routing))
- Decode scheduling for agent traffic: 2.41x ([SemiAnalysis](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/agentx-inferencexv3-does-cuda-moat))
- Cap on long prefills in vLLM: 1.93x ([vLLM team and Inferact](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-09-08-vllm-agentx))
- Re-splitting as traffic shifts: 1.28x ([MIT HAN Lab with Georgia Tech](https://inference-rsi.com))
- Customer-trained speculator: 1.45x ([Together AI](https://www.together.ai/blog/adaptive-learning-speculator-system-atlas))
- Drafter adapted to own traffic: 1.34x ([Decagon](https://x.com/DecagonAI/status/2115511110120120437))
- Draft model tuned on customer traces: 1.2x ([Modal](https://modal.com/blog/trillion-tokens-trillion-parameters))
- Bespoke single-model engine: 1.06x ([Inferact and the vLLM team](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-23-deepseek-v41-flash-pd-wide-ep))

## Open tensions

- **T1** Megakernels: fuse the whole forward pass, or delete the idea? _Settles when:_ Someone runs the same model on the same chip on AgentX with a fused path against a CUDA Graphs plus PDL path, or either camp changes course.
- **T2** Does accumulated knowledge make the optimising agents better, or worse? _Settles when:_ A second team publishes an ablation of machine-accumulated (not hand-curated) memory on a production-scale task.
- **T3** Is this a job for agents, or for plain search? _Settles when:_ A benchmark separates gains from configuration and gains from new code on the same task, or InferenceBench runs a matched-budget search next to the newest agents.
- **T4** Is the moat the traffic, or just the harness? _Settles when:_ A stack tuned only on the public benchmark is deployed on real traffic and someone reports whether the gains hold.
- **T5** Does specialisation stop at the workload class, or go down to each customer? _Settles when:_ A provider publishes per-customer against class-level numbers on the same endpoints.
